title: Rust: Async/Await Fundamentals
description: Understand async/await and Futures in Rust using tokio or futures crate.

steps.title: Basic Async Function
steps.description: Write an async function `async fn say_hello() -> String` that returns `"Hello, async!"`. Use `futures::executor::block_on` to run it. Print the result.
hints: This requires the `futures` crate (simulate without it if needed).

verification.failureMessage: Print 'Hello, async!' from an async-style function.

steps.title: Await Multiple Futures
steps.description: Create two async functions: `compute_one() -> u32` returning 10 and `compute_two() -> u32` returning 20. Call both and sum them, printing the result 30.
hints: Await both futures sequentially or with `join!`.
In Rust, `join!` polls both futures concurrently.

verification.failureMessage: Print the sum of two async computations (30).

steps.title: Async with Sleep
steps.description: Use `tokio::time::sleep` (or simulate) to create a delayed print. Print `"Start"`, wait 100ms (simulated), print `"End"`.
hints: Simulate: print timestamps before and after.

steps.title: Async with .await
steps.description: Write a function `fetch_user(id: u32) -> String` that simulates fetching a user (returns `format!("User {}", id)`). Create two fetches and await them sequentially.

verification.failureMessage: Print two simulated async user fetches.

steps.title: Async Error Handling
steps.description: Write an async function `divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String>`. Create an async function that calls divide with `?` and handles errors. Print success or error messages.
hints: `async fn divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String> { if b == 0.0 { Err("div by zero".into()) } else { Ok(a / b) } }`
Use `?` to propagate errors in async functions.

verification.failureMessage: Handle both success and error cases.
